passages.text: “The sin of Judah is written with an iron stylus, engraved with a diamond point on the tablets of their hearts and on the horns of their altars.
passages.sermon:
Judah is a tribe of Israel.
Judah has sinned.
This sin is permanent.
The sin is written with an iron tool.
The tool has a diamond tip.
The sin is engraved deeply.
The sin is on the tablets of their hearts.
The sin is also on the horns of their altars.
passages.original: חַטַּ֣את יְהוּדָ֗ה כְּתוּבָ֛ה בְּעֵ֥ט בַּרְזֶ֖ל בְּצִפֹּ֣רֶן שָׁמִ֑יר חֲרוּשָׁה֙ עַל־ ל֣וּחַ לִבָּ֔ם וּלְקַרְנ֖וֹת מִזְבְּחוֹתֵיכֶֽם׃

passages.text: Even their children remember their altars and Asherah poles by the green trees and on the high hills.
passages.sermon:
The people of Judah sinned greatly.
Their children remember this sin.
Their children remember the altars their parents built.
Their children remember the Asherah poles their parents set up.
These altars and poles stand by green trees.
These altars and poles stand on high hills.
passages.original: כִּזְכֹּ֤ר בְּנֵיהֶם֙ מִזְבְּחוֹתָ֔ם וַאֲשֵׁרֵיהֶ֖ם עַל־ עֵ֣ץ רַֽעֲנָ֑ן עַ֖ל גְּבָע֥וֹת הַגְּבֹהֽוֹת׃

passages.text: O My mountain in the countryside, I will give over your wealth and all your treasures as plunder, because of the sin of your high places, within all your borders.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Judah.
God calls Judah “My mountain in the countryside.”
God says, “I will give your wealth as plunder.”
I will give all your treasures to others.
I do this because of the sin in your high places.
You have sinned in every part of your land.
passages.original: הֲרָרִי֙ בַּשָּׂדֶ֔ה חֵילְךָ֥ כָל־ אוֹצְרוֹתֶ֖יךָ לָבַ֣ז אֶתֵּ֑ן בָּמֹתֶ֕יךָ בְּחַטָּ֖את בְּכָל־ גְּבוּלֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: And you yourself will relinquish the inheritance that I gave you. I will enslave you to your enemies in a land that you do not know, for you have kindled My anger; it will burn forever.”
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people.
God gave them an inheritance.
They will lose this inheritance.
They will leave behind what God gave them.
God will make them serve their enemies.
Their enemies live in a land they do not know.
God’s people do not know this land.
God’s anger burns against them.
They have made God angry.
God’s anger will burn forever.
passages.original: וְשָׁמַטְתָּ֗ה וּבְךָ֙ מִנַּחֲלָֽתְךָ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נָתַ֣תִּי לָ֔ךְ וְהַעֲבַדְתִּ֙יךָ֙ אֶת־ אֹ֣יְבֶ֔יךָ בָּאָ֖רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹֽא־ יָדָ֑עְתָּ כִּֽי־ אֵ֛שׁ קְדַחְתֶּ֥ם בְּאַפִּ֖י עַד־ עוֹלָ֥ם תּוּקָֽד׃ס

passages.text: This is what the LORD says: “Cursed is the man who trusts in mankind, who makes the flesh his strength and turns his heart from the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD gives a warning.
The LORD says, "Cursed is the man who trusts in mankind."
This man depends on other people for help.
He makes human strength his support.
He turns his heart away from the LORD.
passages.original: כֹּ֣ה׀ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה אָר֤וּר הַגֶּ֙בֶר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִבְטַ֣ח בָּֽאָדָ֔ם וְשָׂ֥ם בָּשָׂ֖ר זְרֹע֑וֹ וּמִן־ יְהוָ֖ה יָס֥וּר לִבּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: He will be like a shrub in the desert; he will not see when prosperity comes. He will dwell in the parched places of the desert, in a salt land where no one lives.
passages.sermon:
A man who trusts in mankind and turns his heart from the LORD will suffer.
He will be like a shrub in the desert.
He will not see when good things come.
He will live in dry, barren places in the wilderness.
He will dwell in a salty land where no one lives.
passages.original: וְהָיָה֙ כְּעַרְעָ֣ר בָּֽעֲרָבָ֔ה וְלֹ֥א יִרְאֶ֖ה כִּי־ יָב֣וֹא ט֑וֹב וְשָׁכַ֤ן חֲרֵרִים֙ בַּמִּדְבָּ֔ר אֶ֥רֶץ מְלֵחָ֖ה וְלֹ֥א תֵשֵֽׁב׃ס

passages.text: But blessed is the man who trusts in the LORD, whose confidence is in Him.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD gives blessings.
A man who trusts in the LORD is blessed.
This man puts his confidence in the LORD.
The LORD is his source of security.
passages.original: בָּר֣וּךְ הַגֶּ֔בֶר אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִבְטַ֖ח בַּֽיהוָ֑ה וְהָיָ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה מִבְטַחֽוֹ׃

passages.text: He is like a tree planted by the waters that sends out its roots toward the stream. It does not fear when the heat comes, and its leaves are always green. It does not worry in a year of drought, nor does it cease to produce fruit.
passages.sermon:
A man who trusts in the LORD is like a tree.
This tree is planted by the waters.
The tree sends its roots toward the stream.
The tree does not fear when heat comes.
Its leaves are always green.
The tree does not worry in a year of drought.
The tree does not stop producing fruit.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֞ה כְּעֵ֣ץ׀ שָׁת֣וּל עַל־ מַ֗יִם וְעַל־ יוּבַל֙ יְשַׁלַּ֣ח שָֽׁרָשָׁ֔יו וְלֹ֤א יִרָא כִּֽי־ יָבֹ֣א חֹ֔ם וְהָיָ֥ה עָלֵ֖הוּ רַֽעֲנָ֑ן וּבִשְׁנַ֤ת בַּצֹּ֙רֶת֙ לֹ֣א יִדְאָ֔ג וְלֹ֥א יָמִ֖ישׁ מֵעֲשׂ֥וֹת פֶּֽרִי׃

passages.text: The heart is deceitful above all things and beyond cure. Who can understand it?
passages.sermon: The human heart is deceitful above all things.\r\nThe heart is beyond cure.\r\nNo one can fully understand the heart.
passages.original: עָקֹ֥ב הַלֵּ֛ב מִכֹּ֖ל וְאָנֻ֣שׁ ה֑וּא מִ֖י יֵדָעֶֽנּוּ׃

passages.text: I, the LORD, search the heart; I examine the mind to reward a man according to his way, by what his deeds deserve.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God.
The LORD searches every heart.
The LORD examines every mind.
The LORD gives each person what he deserves.
The LORD rewards each person for his actions.
The LORD judges each person by his deeds.
passages.original: אֲנִ֧י יְהוָ֛ה חֹקֵ֥ר לֵ֖ב בֹּחֵ֣ן כְּלָי֑וֹת וְלָתֵ֤ת לְאִישׁ֙ כְּדַרְכּוֹ כִּפְרִ֖י מַעֲלָלָֽיו׃ס

passages.text: Like a partridge hatching eggs it did not lay is the man who makes a fortune unjustly. In the middle of his days his riches will desert him, and in the end he will be the fool.”
passages.sermon:
A man may gain wealth by injustice.
He is like a partridge that sits on eggs it did not lay.
His riches do not truly belong to him.
In the middle of his life, his wealth will leave him.
At the end of his life, he will be a fool.
passages.original: קֹרֵ֤א דָגַר֙ וְלֹ֣א יָלָ֔ד עֹ֥שֶׂה עֹ֖שֶׁר וְלֹ֣א בְמִשְׁפָּ֑ט בַּחֲצִ֤י יֹמוֹ יַעַזְבֶ֔נּוּ וּבְאַחֲרִית֖וֹ יִהְיֶ֥ה נָבָֽל׃

passages.text: A glorious throne, exalted from the beginning, is the place of our sanctuary.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is glorious.
His throne is full of glory.
His throne stands high above all things.
His throne has been exalted from the very beginning.
This throne is the place of our sanctuary.
This place is holy.
This place belongs to God.
passages.original: כִּסֵּ֣א כָב֔וֹד מָר֖וֹם מֵֽרִאשׁ֑וֹן מְק֖וֹם מִקְדָּשֵֽׁנוּ׃

passages.text: O LORD, the hope of Israel, all who abandon You will be put to shame. All who turn away will be written in the dust, for they have abandoned the LORD, the fountain of living water.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the hope of Israel.
Anyone who abandons the LORD will be put to shame.
Anyone who turns away from the LORD will be written in the dust.
They have abandoned the LORD.
The LORD is the fountain of living water.
passages.original: מִקְוֵ֤ה יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ יְהוָ֔ה כָּל־ עֹזְבֶ֖יךָ יֵבֹ֑שׁוּ יִסּוֹרַי בָּאָ֣רֶץ יִכָּתֵ֔בוּ כִּ֥י עָזְב֛וּ מְק֥וֹר מַֽיִם־ חַיִּ֖ים אֶת־ יְהוָֽה׃ס

passages.text: Heal me, O LORD, and I will be healed; save me, and I will be saved, for You are my praise.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD has great power to heal.
I ask the LORD to heal me.
If the LORD heals me, I will be healed.
The LORD has power to save.
I ask the LORD to save me.
If the LORD saves me, I will be saved.
The LORD is the one I praise.
passages.original: רְפָאֵ֤נִי יְהוָה֙ וְאֵ֣רָפֵ֔א הוֹשִׁיעֵ֖נִי וְאִוָּשֵׁ֑עָה כִּ֥י תְהִלָּתִ֖י אָֽתָּה׃

passages.text: Behold, they keep saying to me, “Where is the word of the LORD? Let it come now!”
passages.sermon:
People speak to me.
They ask me a question.
They say, “Where is the word of the LORD?”
They say, “Let the word of the LORD come now.”
passages.original: הִנֵּה־ הֵ֕מָּה אֹמְרִ֖ים אֵלָ֑י אַיֵּ֥ה דְבַר־ יְהוָ֖ה יָ֥בוֹא נָֽא׃

passages.text: But I have not run away from being Your shepherd; I have not desired the day of despair. You know that the utterance of my lips was spoken in Your presence.
passages.sermon:
Jeremiah is speaking to God.
Jeremiah says he has not run away from being God's shepherd.
Jeremiah says he has not desired the day of despair.
God knows this.
Jeremiah says God knows what he has spoken.
Jeremiah says his words were spoken in God's presence.
passages.original: וַאֲנִ֞י לֹא־ אַ֣צְתִּי׀ מֵרֹעֶ֣ה אַחֲרֶ֗יךָ וְי֥וֹם אָנ֛וּשׁ לֹ֥א הִתְאַוֵּ֖יתִי אַתָּ֣ה יָדָ֑עְתָּ מוֹצָ֣א שְׂפָתַ֔י נֹ֥כַח פָּנֶ֖יךָ הָיָֽה׃

passages.text: Do not become a terror to me; You are my refuge in the day of disaster.
passages.sermon: The prophet Jeremiah speaks to God.\r\nJeremiah asks God not to become a terror to him.\r\nJeremiah says God is his refuge in the day of disaster.
passages.original: אַל־ תִּֽהְיֵה־ לִ֖י לִמְחִתָּ֑ה מַֽחֲסִי־ אַ֖תָּה בְּי֥וֹם רָעָֽה׃

passages.text: Let my persecutors be put to shame, but do not let me be put to shame. Let them be terrified, but do not let me be terrified. Bring upon them the day of disaster and shatter them with double destruction.
passages.sermon:
Jeremiah is a prophet of God.
Jeremiah has enemies who persecute him.
Let my persecutors be put to shame.
Do not let me be put to shame.
Let them be terrified.
Do not let me be terrified.
Bring the day of disaster upon them.
Shatter them with double destruction.
passages.original: יֵבֹ֤שׁוּ רֹדְפַי֙ וְאַל־ אֵבֹ֣שָׁה אָ֔נִי יֵחַ֣תּוּ הֵ֔מָּה וְאַל־ אֵחַ֖תָּה אָ֑נִי הָבִ֤יא עֲלֵיהֶם֙ י֣וֹם רָעָ֔ה וּמִשְׁנֶ֥ה שִׁבָּר֖וֹן שָׁבְרֵֽם׃ס

passages.text: This is what the LORD said to me: “Go and stand at the gate of the people, through which the kings of Judah go in and out; and stand at all the other gates of Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to me.
He gave me a command.
He said, "Go to the gate of the people."
This is the gate where the kings of Judah enter and leave.
Stand at this gate.
Also, stand at all the other gates of Jerusalem."
passages.original: כֹּה־ אָמַ֨ר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלַ֗י הָלֹ֤ךְ וְעָֽמַדְתָּ֙ בְּשַׁ֣עַר בְּנֵֽי־ עָם אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָבֹ֤אוּ בוֹ֙ מַלְכֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה וַאֲשֶׁ֖ר יֵ֣צְאוּ ב֑וֹ וּבְכֹ֖ל שַׁעֲרֵ֥י יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

passages.text: Say to them, ‘Hear the word of the LORD, O kings of Judah, all people of Judah and Jerusalem who enter through these gates.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Jeremiah.
The LORD gave Jeremiah a message for the people.
Jeremiah must speak to the kings of Judah.
Jeremiah must speak to all the people of Judah.
Jeremiah must speak to all the people living in Jerusalem.
These people enter through the gates of Jerusalem.
Jeremiah must say, “Hear the word of the LORD.”
passages.original: וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲ֠לֵיהֶם שִׁמְע֨וּ דְבַר־ יְהוָ֜ה מַלְכֵ֤י יְהוּדָה֙ וְכָל־ יְהוּדָ֔ה וְכֹ֖ל יֹשְׁבֵ֣י יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם הַבָּאִ֖ים בַּשְּׁעָרִ֥ים הָאֵֽלֶּה׃ס

passages.text: This is what the LORD says: Take heed for yourselves; do not carry a load or bring it through the gates of Jerusalem on the Sabbath day.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is speaking.
The LORD gives a command.
The LORD says, “Be careful to protect your lives.
Do not carry any load on the Sabbath day.
Do not bring a load through the gates of Jerusalem on the Sabbath day.”
passages.original: כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הִשָּׁמְר֖וּ בְּנַפְשֽׁוֹתֵיכֶ֑ם וְאַל־ תִּשְׂא֤וּ מַשָּׂא֙ בְּי֣וֹם הַשַּׁבָּ֔ת וַהֲבֵאתֶ֖ם בְּשַׁעֲרֵ֥י יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

passages.text: You must not carry a load out of your houses or do any work on the Sabbath day, but you must keep the Sabbath day holy, just as I commanded your forefathers.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the people of Judah and Jerusalem.
God gave them a command.
Do not carry any load out of your houses on the Sabbath day.
Do not do any work on the Sabbath day.
Keep the Sabbath day holy.
I, the LORD, commanded your forefathers to do this.
passages.original: וְלֹא־ תוֹצִ֨יאוּ מַשָּׂ֤א מִבָּֽתֵּיכֶם֙ בְּי֣וֹם הַשַּׁבָּ֔ת וְכָל־ מְלָאכָ֖ה לֹ֣א תַֽעֲשׂ֑וּ וְקִדַּשְׁתֶּם֙ אֶת־ י֣וֹם הַשַּׁבָּ֔ת כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוִּ֖יתִי אֶת־ אֲבוֹתֵיכֶֽם׃

passages.text: Yet they would not listen or incline their ear, but they stiffened their necks and would not listen or receive My discipline.
passages.sermon:
The people did not listen to the LORD.
They did not pay attention to His words.
They became stubborn.
They refused to listen.
They refused to accept the LORD’s discipline.
passages.original: וְלֹ֣א שָֽׁמְע֔וּ וְלֹ֥א הִטּ֖וּ אֶת־ אָזְנָ֑ם וַיַּקְשׁוּ֙ אֶת־ עָרְפָּ֔ם לְבִלְתִּ֣י שׁוֹמֵעַ וּלְבִלְתִּ֖י קַ֥חַת מוּסָֽר׃

passages.text: If, however, you listen carefully to Me, says the LORD, and bring no load through the gates of this city on the Sabbath day, and keep the Sabbath day holy, and do no work on it, then kings and princes will enter through the gates of this city. They will sit on the throne of David, riding in chariots and on horses with their officials, along with the men of Judah and the residents of Jerusalem, and this city will be inhabited forever.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to the people of Jerusalem.
He says, “If you listen carefully to Me,
and if you do not bring any load through the gates of this city on the Sabbath day,
and if you keep the Sabbath day holy,
and if you do no work on the Sabbath day,
then kings and princes will enter through the gates of this city.
These kings and princes will sit on the throne of David.
They will ride in chariots and on horses.
Their officials will be with them.
The men of Judah and the residents of Jerusalem will also be with them.
This city will be inhabited forever.
passages.original: וְ֠הָיָה אִם־ שָׁמֹ֨עַ תִּשְׁמְע֤וּן אֵלַי֙ נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֔ה לְבִלְתִּ֣י׀ הָבִ֣יא מַשָּׂ֗א בְּשַׁעֲרֵ֛י הָעִ֥יר הַזֹּ֖את בְּי֣וֹם הַשַּׁבָּ֑ת וּלְקַדֵּשׁ֙ אֶת־ י֣וֹם הַשַּׁבָּ֔ת לְבִלְתִּ֥י עֲשֽׂוֹת־ בֹּה כָּל־ מְלָאכָֽה׃ וּבָ֣אוּ בְשַׁעֲרֵ֣י הָעִ֣יר הַזֹּ֡את מְלָכִ֣ים׀ וְשָׂרִ֡ים יֹשְׁבִים֩ עַל־ כִּסֵּ֨א דָוִ֜ד רֹכְבִ֣ים׀ בָּרֶ֣כֶב וּבַסּוּסִ֗ים הֵ֚מָּה וְשָׂ֣רֵיהֶ֔ם אִ֥ישׁ יְהוּדָ֖ה וְיֹשְׁבֵ֣י יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְיָשְׁבָ֥ה הָֽעִיר־ הַזֹּ֖את לְעוֹלָֽם׃

passages.text: And people will come from the cities of Judah and the places around Jerusalem, from the land of Benjamin, and from the foothills, the hill country, and the Negev, bringing burnt offerings and sacrifices, grain offerings and frankincense, and thank offerings to the house of the LORD.
passages.sermon:
People will come from the cities of Judah.
People will come from the areas around Jerusalem.
People will come from the land of Benjamin.
People will come from the foothills.
People will come from the hill country.
People will come from the Negev.
They will bring burnt offerings to the house of the LORD.
They will bring sacrifices to the house of the LORD.
They will bring grain offerings to the house of the LORD.
They will bring frankincense to the house of the LORD.
They will bring thank offerings to the house of the LORD.

passages.text: But if you do not listen to Me to keep the Sabbath day holy by not carrying a load while entering the gates of Jerusalem on the Sabbath day, then I will kindle an unquenchable fire in its gates to consume the citadels of Jerusalem.’ ”
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to the people of Jerusalem.
He commands them to keep the Sabbath day holy.
He tells them not to carry any load through the gates of Jerusalem on the Sabbath day.
He warns them about disobedience.
If you do not listen to Me,
If you do not keep the Sabbath day holy,
If you carry a load through the gates of Jerusalem on the Sabbath day,
Then I will start a fire in its gates.
This fire will burn the palaces of Jerusalem.
No one will be able to put out this fire.
